interest: Japanese propaganda spread by Montevideo's mayor, 1930s.
overview: Decimal file 894.20233 comprises State Department cross-reference sheets and a military intelligence report from 1934 to 1939 monitoring Japanese commercial, agricultural, and propaganda activities in Uruguay. The file documents inquiries into rumored Japanese schemes to establish manufacturing centers and cotton spinning mills in the Free Zone of Colonia and Isla Libertad, confirming instead modest agricultural land purchases near the town of Libertad. It also includes an intelligence report by Military Attaché Col. Lester Baker on English-language propaganda pamphlets issued by the Foreign Affairs Association of Japan justifying the Sino-Japanese War, which were distributed in Montevideo by its Mayor, who operated an import-export firm trading with Japan, alongside tracking the parliamentary ratification of the 1934 Japan-Uruguay Treaty of Commerce and Navigation.

subfiles.about: Indexes a letter regarding rumored Japanese schemes to transform the Free Zone of Colonia into a manufacturing base.

subfiles.about: Summarizes an investigation finding rumors of a Japanese cotton spinning mill concession on Isla Libertad to be groundless, while noting land purchases near Libertad.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: no Japanese mill concession on Isla Libertad, but Japanese bought land near Libertad.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Investigation of Rumored Japanese Concession on Isla Libertad

subfiles.about: Reports that the Uruguayan Ministry of Industries and Labor has no knowledge of any Japanese concession on Liberty Island.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Uruguay's ministry knows of no Japanese concession on Liberty Island.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Uruguayan Ministry of Industries Statement on Liberty Island Concession

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese propaganda pamphlets defending military intervention in China and describes their distribution in Montevideo by the city's mayor.
subfiles.summary: Colonel Lester Baker reports Mayor Zanni of Montevideo distributing Japanese pamphlets justifying the China war.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Report: Japanese Propaganda Justifying Chinese Adventure

subfiles.about: Records the approval by the Uruguayan Senate and forthcoming ratification of the 1934 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Uruguay's Senate approved the 1934 Japan-Uruguay trade treaty in 1939.
